newsitem.title: USA: Profit growth seen slower at U.S. brokerages in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Profit growth seen slower at U.S. brokerages in Q1.

text.p: U.S. brokerages are expected to report solid quarterly earnings in the coming weeks, but analysts are not counting on the kind of booming profit growth the firms posted the last two years.

Some early reporting firms like Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc have surprised Wall Street with strong quarterly numbers, but analysts noted that the results failed to account for the sharp decline in financial markets that occurred in March.
"January was a good month but the market peaked out in February and we've had a slide since then," said Perrin Long, an independent analyst who covers the financial industry.
Lehman and Morgan Stanley Group Inc, whose quarters ended in February, "got a little help" the other firms will not share, he said.
Because some firms rely heavily on proprietary trading for their profits -- Salomon Inc is an example -- estimating earnings from quarter to quarter is a tricky business.
But a look at estimates across the industry shows that analysts do not believe the brokerages will improve much on their results of a quarter or year ago.
For example, according to information provided by First Call, analysts expect Merrill Lynch and Co Inc will report first quarter earnings of $2.01 per share.
That would represent a decline from both the $2.27 per share Merrill earned in the fourth quarter of 1996 as well as the $2.03 per share it earned in the first quarter last year.
For the investment banks, some of the reduction can be tied to a slowdown in the initial public offering arena, a powerful source of fees early last year.
Analysts said the market decline may also result in a drag on retail-oriented brokerages, whose customers may have adopted a more cautious approach than in the recent past.
